en.title: Chain of Command (Tree DFS Order, k-th Receiver)
en.description:
You are given a tree rooted at 0, with parent[0]=-1. A notification sent to node p propagates in preorder DFS order, and the children of each node are visited in ascending order of number. Each query (p,k) returns the k-th node in the preorder sequence of p's subtree (1-based, including p); if k exceeds the subtree size, return -1.

This site adds the standard input/output protocol; it does not mean the original site's function-style problem had this protocol.
en.input: n; one line of n parent values; q; then q lines of p k. Node numbers and p in queries are 0-based. By convention parent[0]=-1, and the parent array represents a valid tree rooted at 0. This site adds n≤200000, q≤200000.
en.output: Output the answers in query order, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the full approach, proof and complexity.
hints: Use iterative DFS to build the preorder sequence of the whole tree, and record the contiguous range of each subtree.
